model.note: Shipped weights are a starting guess, not a fit: nobody's movie ratings were available when the catalogue was built. Rate eight films the Oracle knows and use Recalibrate in Settings to fit them to your own taste.

catalog.title: Halloween
catalog.hook: On Halloween night a boy who killed his sister at six comes home to Haddonfield, fifteen years older and wearing a white mask, and fixes on a babysitter named Laurie.
catalog.caution: Almost nothing happens for the first hour except Michael watching; if you need kills early, the patience it asks for can read as slow.

catalog.title: The Shining
catalog.hook: A blocked writer takes the winter caretaker job at a mountain hotel with his wife and son, and the hotel starts working on him.
catalog.caution: It is cold and long and leaves its mysteries unexplained; if you want the rules of the haunting spelled out, Kubrick refuses.

catalog.title: Alien
catalog.hook: The crew of a towing ship answer a distress call on a dead moon and bring something back aboard.
catalog.caution: The first forty minutes are deliberately industrial and quiet; it is a slow burn before it is a monster movie.

catalog.title: Aliens
catalog.hook: Fifty-seven years after the Nostromo, Ripley goes back to the moon with a squad of marines, because the colony there has stopped answering.
catalog.caution: It trades dread for firepower; anyone who loved the first film's silence may find this one loud.

catalog.title: The Thing
catalog.hook: Twelve men at an Antarctic research station take in a dog fleeing a Norwegian camp, and something that can wear any of them gets loose.
catalog.caution: There are no women and almost no warmth; the characters are tools for paranoia rather than people you get to know.

catalog.title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
catalog.hook: The teenagers of Elm Street are dying in their sleep, and Nancy realises the burned man in her dreams is real enough to kill.
catalog.caution: The effects are 1984 rubber and the acting outside Heather Langenkamp is shaky; it plays better as a ride than as a story.

catalog.title: The Exorcist
catalog.hook: A twelve-year-old in Georgetown starts changing, the doctors find nothing, and her mother turns to a priest who is losing his faith.
catalog.caution: It spends a long time on medical procedures and a priest's grief before the possession takes over; the famous scenes are a small part of the film.

catalog.title: Hereditary
catalog.hook: After her secretive mother dies, a miniature artist and her family start to come apart, and what she inherited turns out to be worse than grief.
catalog.caution: It is a family tragedy for an hour before it is a horror film, and it is genuinely upsetting; this is not a fun watch with friends.

catalog.title: Midsommar
catalog.hook: A grieving woman tags along with her distant boyfriend to a midsummer festival in rural Sweden that happens once every ninety years.
catalog.caution: It is two and a half hours in daylight, more breakup film than scare machine; the dread is slow and the payoff is strange rather than frightening.

catalog.title: Get Out
catalog.hook: Chris goes upstate to meet his white girlfriend's liberal parents for the weekend, and everyone at the house is a little too pleased to see him.
catalog.caution: The scares are few and the satire is pointed; if you want a haunted-house fright, this is a thriller first.

catalog.title: Scream
catalog.hook: A year after her mother's murder, Sidney Prescott's town gets a masked killer who phones his victims and quizzes them on horror movies.
catalog.caution: It winks at the audience constantly; if meta-commentary pulls you out of a film, the jokes will cost it some menace.

catalog.title: Scream 2
catalog.hook: Sidney is at college, a film of her ordeal has just opened, and a new Ghostface starts killing at the premiere.
catalog.caution: It is looser and sillier than the first, and the reveal is the weakest of the early films.

catalog.title: The Babadook
catalog.hook: A widowed mother, worn to nothing by her difficult son, reads him a pop-up book that should not be in the house.
catalog.caution: The child is shrill by design and the first half is exhausting to sit through; it is about grief more than a monster.

catalog.title: It Follows
catalog.hook: After sleeping with a new boyfriend, Jay is followed, at walking pace, by something only she can see, and it will not stop until it reaches her.
catalog.caution: The rules are never fully explained and the ending is open; the dread is the point, not the answers.

catalog.title: The Witch
catalog.hook: In 1630s New England a Puritan family banished from their plantation settle at the edge of a wood, and the baby vanishes while their eldest daughter is watching him.
catalog.caution: The dialogue is period English and hard to follow at first, and it is all atmosphere until the end.

catalog.title: The Conjuring
catalog.hook: In 1971 the paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren take the case of a Rhode Island family whose new farmhouse is turning on them.
catalog.caution: It is classic haunted-house machinery done very well, but it is machinery; nothing here will surprise a seasoned viewer.

catalog.title: Insidious
catalog.hook: A boy falls into a coma that doctors cannot explain, and the house the family moves into to escape their grief is not the problem.
catalog.caution: The last act goes somewhere theatrical and a little silly; the first hour is the frightening part.

catalog.title: The Ring
catalog.hook: A Seattle journalist investigates a videotape that seems to kill whoever watches it seven days later, and then her son watches it.
catalog.caution: It is more investigation than terror for long stretches, and the mystery's logic is loose.

catalog.title: Ringu
catalog.hook: A reporter chasing an urban legend about a cursed videotape watches it, gets the phone call, and has a week.
catalog.caution: It is quieter and slower than the American remake; the scares are rationed and the famous one is near the end.

catalog.title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
catalog.hook: Five friends driving through rural Texas pick up a hitchhiker and stop at the wrong house.
catalog.caution: It is grimy, shrill and relentless, with almost no characterisation; the final act is forty minutes of screaming.

catalog.title: Night of the Living Dead
catalog.hook: Strangers barricade themselves in a Pennsylvania farmhouse as the recently dead start walking and eating the living.
catalog.caution: It is black and white, low budget and stagey indoors; the power is in the bleakness and the ending, not the effects.

catalog.title: Dawn of the Dead
catalog.hook: Four survivors of the zombie outbreak hole up in an abandoned shopping mall and, for a while, live the dream.
catalog.caution: It is long and the middle is a lazy consumerist idyll on purpose; the satire can feel like padding.

catalog.title: The Evil Dead
catalog.hook: Five friends at a cabin in Tennessee find a book bound in human skin and a tape recorder, and play the tape.
catalog.caution: It is raw, cheap and includes an infamous assault by trees that many viewers find gratuitous.
contentWarnings: sexual assault by a possessed tree

catalog.title: Evil Dead II
catalog.hook: Ash goes back to the cabin, the dead wake again, and his own hand turns against him.
catalog.caution: It is slapstick as much as horror; if you came for scares, the cartoon energy undercuts them.

catalog.title: Rosemary's Baby
catalog.hook: A young wife moves into a grand Manhattan building with her actor husband, gets pregnant, and the friendly old neighbours take a close interest.
catalog.caution: Almost nothing overtly frightening happens; it is two hours of mounting gaslighting, which some find more maddening than scary.

catalog.title: Psycho
catalog.hook: A secretary steals forty thousand dollars, drives off into the rain, and checks into a quiet motel run by a shy young man and his mother.
catalog.caution: Its twists are so famous you may know them already, and the closing psychiatrist scene is a creaky lecture.

catalog.title: The Silence of the Lambs
catalog.hook: An FBI trainee is sent to interview an imprisoned cannibal psychiatrist, because he may be able to help catch a killer who skins women.
catalog.caution: It is grim and procedural; the horror is psychological and the gore comes in short, hard shocks.

catalog.title: Jaws
catalog.hook: A great white starts taking swimmers off a New England resort island just before the Fourth of July, and the mayor will not close the beaches.
catalog.caution: The second half is three men on a boat talking; if you wanted constant shark, it is famously rationed.

catalog.title: An American Werewolf in London
catalog.hook: Two American backpackers are attacked on the Yorkshire moors; one dies, and the other wakes up in a London hospital having very bad dreams.
catalog.caution: The tone swings hard between jokes and gore, and the ending is abrupt.

catalog.title: The Fly
catalog.hook: An eccentric scientist tests his teleporter on himself without noticing a housefly in the pod.
catalog.caution: The body horror is extreme and slow, and it ends in tragedy rather than triumph.

catalog.title: Carrie
catalog.hook: A bullied teenage girl with a fanatically religious mother discovers she can move things with her mind, just before prom.
catalog.caution: The famous climax is late and the build is mostly cruelty to watch; the split-screen style is very 1976.

catalog.title: Suspiria
catalog.hook: An American ballet student arrives at a German dance academy on a stormy night and realises the faculty are not just teachers.
catalog.caution: The plot is thin and the dubbing odd; it is a fever dream of colour and sound rather than a story.

catalog.title: The Descent
catalog.hook: A year after a tragedy, six women go caving in the Appalachians, and the cave is not on any map.
catalog.caution: Claustrophobia is a feature, not a bug: if tight spaces get to you this will be miserable, and the ending is bleak.

catalog.title: 28 Days Later
catalog.hook: A bicycle courier wakes from a coma in an empty London twenty-eight days after a rage virus has torn the country apart.
catalog.caution: The last act at the soldiers' mansion is where the real horror is, and it is ugly in a different way.

catalog.title: Train to Busan
catalog.hook: A workaholic father takes his small daughter on the train from Seoul to Busan the morning a zombie outbreak boards with them.
catalog.caution: It is subtitled and it will make you cry; the father's arc is predictable even when the set pieces are not.

catalog.title: The Cabin in the Woods
catalog.hook: Five college friends go to a remote cabin for the weekend, and two men in a control room are watching.
catalog.caution: It is a puzzle box about horror movies more than a horror movie; it is not trying to scare you much.

catalog.title: Shaun of the Dead
catalog.hook: A London electronics salesman with a dead-end life tries to win back his girlfriend and save his mum, during a zombie apocalypse.
catalog.caution: It is a comedy first; the horror is affectionate and the scares are mostly gags.

catalog.title: What We Do in the Shadows
catalog.hook: A documentary crew follows four vampire flatmates in Wellington as they argue about the dishes and prepare for the Unholy Masquerade.
catalog.caution: Deadpan mockumentary is a specific taste; if it does not land in the first ten minutes it will not.

catalog.title: Tucker & Dale vs Evil
catalog.hook: Two gentle hillbillies fixing up their holiday cabin are mistaken for killers by college kids, who keep dying trying to stop them.
catalog.caution: It is one joke, well told; if the premise does not amuse you, the gore will not carry it.

catalog.title: The Orphanage
catalog.hook: A woman reopens the seaside orphanage where she grew up as a home for sick children, and her adopted son starts playing with friends no one else can see.
catalog.caution: It is a ghost story about a mother's grief, and it is heartbreaking rather than thrilling.

catalog.title: Pan's Labyrinth
catalog.hook: In 1944 Spain a girl sent to live with her mother's new husband, a fascist captain, follows a faun into a labyrinth that sets her three tasks.
catalog.caution: The fairy tale is the smaller half; the real-world cruelty is brutal and the film is far darker than its posters.

catalog.title: The Others
catalog.hook: On Jersey in 1945 a mother keeps her two light-sensitive children in a dark mansion, until new servants arrive and the house fills with sounds.
catalog.caution: It is slow, quiet and built for one final turn; if you guess it, much of the tension goes.

catalog.title: The Sixth Sense
catalog.hook: A child psychologist takes on a frightened eight-year-old who says he sees dead people.
catalog.caution: The twist is so well known it may be spoiled for you; without it, this is a gentle, sad drama with a few jolts.

catalog.title: A Quiet Place
catalog.hook: A family survives in near silence on a farm, because the creatures that ended the world hunt by sound, and the mother is pregnant.
catalog.caution: The logic gaps are big if you go looking for them, and the opening is a gut punch.

catalog.title: Us
catalog.hook: On a beach holiday in Santa Cruz, a family finds four people standing in their driveway who look exactly like them.
catalog.caution: The last act explains its mythology at length and the explanation raises more questions than it answers.

catalog.title: Nope
catalog.hook: Siblings running a struggling horse ranch for Hollywood productions notice something in the sky over their gulch, and decide to film it.
catalog.caution: It is a spectacle film about spectacle, slow in the middle, and the chimp subplot is upsetting and never explained.

catalog.title: Barbarian
catalog.hook: A woman arrives at her Detroit rental late at night to find it double-booked, and the stranger already there seems nice.
catalog.caution: It swerves hard twice and the second swerve is a different film; the subject underneath is grim.

catalog.title: Talk to Me
catalog.hook: Teenagers in Adelaide pass round an embalmed hand that lets the dead possess you for ninety seconds, and film it for the group chat.
catalog.caution: It is genuinely cruel to its youngest character and the grief subplot is heavy; it is not a party movie.

catalog.title: Smile
catalog.hook: A psychiatrist watches a patient die in front of her, smiling, and starts seeing the smile everywhere.
catalog.caution: It leans heavily on jump scares and runs long; the mental-health metaphor is not subtle.

catalog.title: X
catalog.hook: In 1979 a crew rents a guesthouse on an elderly couple's Texas farm to shoot an adult film, without telling the hosts.
catalog.caution: It is very explicit about sex as well as violence, and takes its time before the killing starts.

catalog.title: Pearl
catalog.hook: On the same Texas farm in 1918, a young woman with a sick father and a cold mother dreams of being a star, and will do anything to get there.
catalog.caution: It is more character study than slasher, and its Technicolor brightness keeps the violence strange rather than scary.

catalog.title: Ready or Not
catalog.hook: On her wedding night a bride agrees to play hide and seek with her new husband's rich family, who have to kill her before dawn.
catalog.caution: It is a black comedy with a simple premise; it does not dig deep and it does not try to.

catalog.title: The Invisible Man
catalog.hook: Two weeks after Cecilia escapes her controlling tech-genius boyfriend, he is reported dead, and she is sure he is still in the room.
catalog.caution: It is about abuse and gaslighting, and watching nobody believe her is draining by design.

catalog.title: Annihilation
catalog.hook: A biologist joins four other women on an expedition into the Shimmer, a zone where her husband's last team vanished and nature has gone wrong.
catalog.caution: It is cerebral and ambiguous and the ending is abstract; if you want answers, it withholds them.

catalog.title: The Wailing
catalog.hook: A bumbling village policeman investigates a wave of killings and sickness that the villagers blame on a Japanese stranger in the hills.
catalog.caution: It is two and a half hours, subtitled, tonally all over the place for its first hour, and deliberately unresolved.

catalog.title: Poltergeist
catalog.hook: In a new suburban development the youngest Freeling daughter starts talking to the television, and then the house takes her.
catalog.caution: It is a family film with teeth, closer to Spielberg than to a nasty horror movie.

catalog.title: Gremlins
catalog.hook: A boy gets an adorable creature for Christmas with three rules, and breaks all of them.
catalog.caution: It is a family movie with a mean streak, and the middle is more mayhem than plot.
contentWarnings: a monologue about a dead father

catalog.title: Beetlejuice
catalog.hook: A newly dead couple try to scare the awful new owners out of their house and hire a bio-exorcist who turns out to be much worse.
catalog.caution: Beetlejuice is barely in it and the plot is a sketch; it is all design and anarchy.

catalog.title: Interview with the Vampire
catalog.hook: A two-hundred-year-old vampire tells a reporter about the companion who made him and the child they made together.
catalog.caution: Louis broods for most of it and the story wanders across centuries; it is lush and mournful rather than scary.
contentWarnings: a child turned into a vampire

catalog.title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
catalog.hook: Jonathan Harker travels to Transylvania to sell a London house to a count who has seen his long-dead love in Jonathan's fiancée.
catalog.caution: Keanu Reeves's accent is a famous casualty and the tone is operatic to the point of camp.
contentWarnings: a baby is fed to vampires

catalog.title: Let the Right One In
catalog.hook: In a snowbound Stockholm suburb in 1982 a bullied twelve-year-old befriends the strange girl who has just moved in next door and only comes out at night.
catalog.caution: It is quiet, cold and subtitled, and it leaves the most disturbing implications for you to work out.

catalog.title: Crimson Peak
catalog.hook: A young American writer marries a charming English baronet and moves to his crumbling, clay-red mansion, where the ghosts are trying to warn her.
catalog.caution: It is a gothic romance more than a ghost story, and the mystery is easy to see coming.

catalog.title: The Autopsy of Jane Doe
catalog.hook: A father-and-son coroner team take in an unidentified woman found buried in a basement and begin the autopsy as a storm sets in.
catalog.caution: The last act explains too much; the first hour, on the table, is the best of it.

catalog.title: Sinister
catalog.hook: A true-crime writer moves his family into a house where a family was murdered, and finds a box of home movies in the attic.
catalog.caution: Ethan Hawke's character is hard to like and the film is very dark; the found footage reels are the scariest part.

catalog.title: The Blair Witch Project
catalog.hook: Three film students hike into the Maryland woods in 1994 to make a documentary about a local legend, and their footage is found a year later.
catalog.caution: It is shaky, shouty and shows nothing; if the found-footage form leaves you cold, there is nothing else here.

catalog.title: REC
catalog.hook: A TV reporter shadowing the Barcelona fire brigade for the night follows them into an apartment building that is then sealed by the authorities.
catalog.caution: It is shaky handheld footage throughout and the final explanation is rushed.

catalog.title: The Lighthouse
catalog.hook: Two lighthouse keepers on a remote New England rock in the 1890s get stranded by a storm and slowly lose their minds together.
catalog.caution: It is black and white, square, grotesque and intentionally obscure; it is a mood more than a story.

catalog.title: Saint Maud
catalog.hook: A pious young hospice nurse takes on a dying dancer as her patient and becomes convinced she has to save the woman's soul.
catalog.caution: It is short and spare and very unsettling, and its ending is designed to stay with you uncomfortably.

catalog.title: Raw
catalog.hook: A lifelong vegetarian starts veterinary school, is made to eat a raw rabbit kidney in a hazing ritual, and develops a new hunger.
catalog.caution: The body horror is visceral and the animal scenes are hard; it is a coming-of-age film that happens to be about cannibalism.

catalog.title: Ginger Snaps
catalog.hook: Two death-obsessed teenage sisters in a Canadian suburb get attacked on the night of Ginger's first period, and Ginger starts to change.
catalog.caution: The budget shows in the creature work, and the sisters are deliberately abrasive.

catalog.title: Jennifer's Body
catalog.hook: After a botched occult ritual by an indie band, a high school's most popular girl starts eating the boys, and her best friend is the only one who notices.
catalog.caution: The tone wobbles between teen comedy and horror and neither is very frightening.

catalog.title: The Lost Boys
catalog.hook: Two brothers move with their mother to a California boardwalk town where a gang of young vampires runs the night.
catalog.caution: It is a very 1987 teen movie with a saxophone; the horror is mostly for fun.

catalog.title: Fright Night
catalog.hook: A teenager is certain the new neighbour is a vampire, and the only person who will help is a washed-up TV horror host.
catalog.caution: It is campy and the effects are of their era; it plays as a romp.

catalog.title: Hellraiser
catalog.hook: A woman's lover, torn apart by beings from another dimension, is regenerating under the floorboards, and needs her to bring him blood.
catalog.caution: The Cenobites are barely in it; it is an ugly domestic melodrama with flayed skin, and the effects are dated.

catalog.title: Candyman
catalog.hook: A Chicago graduate student researching urban legends in the Cabrini-Green projects says his name five times in the mirror.
catalog.caution: The third act gets messy, and its handling of race was criticised then and since.

catalog.title: Terrifier
catalog.hook: On Halloween night two young women leaving a party cross paths with Art the Clown, who does not speak.
catalog.caution: There is very little story and the gore is the whole point; it is extreme even for a slasher.

catalog.title: Weapons
catalog.hook: At 2:17 one morning, every child in one teacher's class but one gets up, walks out into the dark and vanishes.
catalog.caution: It is told in overlapping chapters from different people, and the explanation, when it comes, is pulpier than the build-up.

catalog.title: Sinners
catalog.hook: Twin brothers come home to 1932 Mississippi to open a juke joint, and on opening night something comes to the door asking to be invited in.
catalog.caution: It is an hour of music and character before the vampires arrive; if you want the siege early, it makes you wait.

catalog.title: Longlegs
catalog.hook: An FBI agent with a strange intuition is assigned the decades-old case of a killer who leaves coded letters at family murder-suicides.
catalog.caution: It is all oppressive mood; the procedural turns supernatural and the ending is more unsettling than satisfying.

catalog.title: The Substance
catalog.hook: A fading TV fitness star takes a black-market drug that creates a younger, better version of herself, on strict condition that they share their time.
catalog.caution: It is long, extreme and deliberately grotesque, and it has no interest in subtlety.

catalog.title: Nosferatu
catalog.hook: In 1838 a young estate agent travels to the Carpathians to close a sale, leaving behind a wife who has been haunted since girlhood by something calling her name.
catalog.caution: It is slow and suffocating and the period dialogue is heavy; it is closer to a nightmare than an adventure.

catalog.title: Late Night with the Devil
catalog.hook: On Halloween night 1977 a struggling talk-show host goes live with a girl said to be possessed, presented as recovered master tapes.
catalog.caution: The found-footage frame breaks its own rules in places and the ending is busy.

catalog.title: The Mist
catalog.hook: After a storm a strange mist rolls into a small Maine town, trapping a father, his son and a supermarket of strangers inside with whatever is in it.
catalog.caution: The ending is one of the bleakest ever put in a studio film, and the human villains are more exhausting than the monsters.

catalog.title: Misery
catalog.hook: A novelist crashes his car in a Colorado blizzard and is rescued by his number one fan, who is not happy about what he did to her favourite character.
catalog.caution: It is mostly two people in one house; the tension is psychological until a few very physical moments.

catalog.title: It
catalog.hook: In the summer of 1989 seven outcast kids in Derry, Maine, discover they are all being hunted by the same thing, and it often looks like a clown.
catalog.caution: It leans on loud jump scares, and the threats to the children from adults are harder to watch than Pennywise.
contentWarnings: implied sexual abuse of a child

catalog.title: Coraline
catalog.hook: A bored girl in a new house finds a small door to a better version of her life, where her Other Mother wants her to stay and sew buttons on her eyes.
catalog.caution: It is a children's film; scary for kids, eerie rather than frightening for adults.

catalog.title: Frankenstein
catalog.hook: A young scientist stitches together a man from the dead and brings him to life in a storm, and then abandons him.
catalog.caution: It is seventy minutes, early-sound stiff, and its frights are historical rather than current.

catalog.title: Bride of Frankenstein
catalog.hook: Frankenstein's creature survived the fire, and a stranger, stranger scientist forces Henry to build him a mate.
catalog.caution: It is camp and sweet more than scary, and the Bride is in it for about five minutes.

catalog.title: Cure
catalog.hook: A Tokyo detective investigates murders committed by ordinary people who carve an X into their victims and have no idea why they did it.
catalog.caution: It is glacial and deliberately withholding; the horror is in long still shots and what is never explained.

catalog.title: Audition
catalog.hook: A widower holds a fake film audition to find a new wife and falls for a quiet former ballerina, whose references do not check out.
catalog.caution: For an hour it is a gentle romance; the last half-hour is torture, and it is very hard to watch.

catalog.title: Tremors
catalog.hook: Two handymen in a Nevada desert town are about to leave for good when the residents start getting eaten from below.
catalog.caution: It is pure B-movie fun with no depth; it does not pretend otherwise.

catalog.title: The Return of the Living Dead
catalog.hook: Two warehouse workers in Louisville accidentally release a gas from an army canister, and the cemetery next door wakes up wanting brains.
catalog.caution: It is punk, crude and silly; the characters are there to be eaten.

catalog.title: Re-Animator
catalog.hook: A medical student's new lodger has a glowing green serum that brings the dead back, badly.
catalog.caution: It is gleefully tasteless and includes a notorious sexual assault by a severed head.
comps: The Return of the Living Dead

catalog.title: Black Christmas
catalog.hook: Over the Christmas break the women of a sorority house start getting obscene phone calls, and one of them goes missing.
catalog.caution: It is slow and talky between scares, but it is one of the films that invented the slasher.

catalog.title: The Fog
catalog.hook: On its hundredth anniversary a California fishing town is wrapped in a glowing fog, and inside it are the men the town's founders drowned.
catalog.caution: It is a campfire story stretched to feature length, with a sprawling cast and little depth.

catalog.title: They Live
catalog.hook: A drifter finds sunglasses that show him the truth: the rich are aliens and every billboard says OBEY.
catalog.caution: It is blunt satire with a five-minute alley fight; subtle it is not.

catalog.title: In the Mouth of Madness
catalog.hook: An insurance investigator hunts for a missing horror novelist whose books are making readers go mad, and finds the town from the novels.
catalog.caution: It is loopy and gleefully meta; if you need things to add up, they do not.

catalog.title: Hush
catalog.hook: A deaf writer living alone in the woods discovers a masked man outside her window, and he has decided to play with her first.
catalog.caution: It is a single-location home-invasion film; the killer is a man in a mask, not a mystery.

catalog.title: Gerald's Game
catalog.hook: A couple's getaway goes wrong when her husband dies of a heart attack, leaving her handcuffed to the bed in a remote house.
catalog.caution: It turns into a reckoning with childhood abuse, and it contains one of the most graphic injury scenes in recent horror.

catalog.title: Speak No Evil
catalog.hook: A polite Danish family accept an invitation to visit a Dutch couple they met on holiday, and are too polite to leave.
catalog.caution: It is an exercise in excruciating social discomfort with an ending that many viewers find unbearable.

catalog.title: Fresh
catalog.hook: Fed up with dating apps, Noa meets a charming surgeon in a supermarket, and agrees to a weekend away.
catalog.caution: The opening credits arrive half an hour in; it is a dark satire of dating and its gross-out moments are more icky than scary.

catalog.title: Bodies Bodies Bodies
catalog.hook: Rich twenty-somethings riding out a hurricane in a mansion play a murder game, and then someone actually dies.
catalog.caution: The characters are insufferable on purpose; it is a satire of Gen Z talk as much as a whodunit.

catalog.title: Happy Death Day
catalog.hook: A self-absorbed college student is murdered by a masked killer on her birthday, wakes up that morning again, and has to solve her own death.
catalog.caution: It is PG-13 and light; the horror is a frame for a comedy about becoming a better person.

catalog.title: Freaky
catalog.hook: A shy teenager swaps bodies with the local serial killer the night before homecoming, and has twenty-four hours to swap back.
catalog.caution: It is a body-swap comedy with gory kills; there is no real dread.

catalog.title: The Haunting
catalog.hook: An anthropologist invites a lonely, fragile woman to Hill House to help him prove it is haunted, and the house chooses her.
catalog.caution: Nothing is ever shown; the terror is sound and suggestion, and the narration is heavy.

catalog.title: The Innocents
catalog.hook: A governess takes charge of two orphaned children at a vast country estate and begins to believe the previous staff, both dead, have not let them go.
catalog.caution: It is black and white, restrained and ambiguous by design; you have to decide what is really happening.

catalog.title: The Wicker Man
catalog.hook: A devout police sergeant flies to a remote Scottish island to find a missing girl, and the islanders tell him she never existed.
catalog.caution: It is partly a musical, and the folk songs and pagan comedy can seem silly until the final ten minutes.

catalog.title: Don't Look Now
catalog.hook: Grieving their drowned daughter, a couple go to Venice in winter, where a blind psychic tells the wife the girl is happy and her husband is in danger.
catalog.caution: It is elliptical, cut in fragments, and devastatingly sad; it is not built for thrills.

catalog.title: Event Horizon
catalog.hook: A rescue crew is sent to Neptune to recover an experimental ship that vanished seven years ago and has just come back from somewhere.
catalog.caution: The script is clunky and the gore is extreme in brief flashes; it is hellish rather than smart.

catalog.title: Pet Sematary
catalog.hook: A doctor moves his family to rural Maine, next to a road with fast trucks and a burial ground the locals say brings things back.
catalog.caution: It is mean and sad in equal measure, the acting is uneven, and the death of a toddler is central.

catalog.title: Trick 'r Treat
catalog.hook: Four interlocking Halloween stories in one small Ohio town, all watched by a little trick-or-treater in a burlap mask who enforces the rules.
catalog.caution: It is an anthology, so some stories land harder than others, and a few children do not survive.

catalog.title: The Love Witch
catalog.hook: A beautiful modern-day witch moves to a small California town and uses love magic to find a man, with fatal results for the men.
catalog.caution: It is a deadpan pastiche of 1960s Technicolor melodrama; if the stilted style does not charm you, two hours is long.

catalog.title: The Host
catalog.hook: A creature mutated by chemicals dumped in the Han River snatches a snack vendor's daughter, and her ramshackle family goes after her.
catalog.caution: It flips between slapstick, satire and tragedy without warning; the tone is the point and also the hurdle.

catalog.title: Friday the 13th
catalog.hook: Camp counsellors reopen Camp Crystal Lake, which closed after a boy drowned there decades ago, and start dying one by one.
catalog.caution: The characters are thin and the acting thinner; it is a kill-count movie with a great final reveal.

catalog.title: The Craft
catalog.hook: A new girl at a Los Angeles Catholic school falls in with three outcasts who practise witchcraft, and their spells start working too well.
catalog.caution: It is a 1996 teen movie through and through, and the last act tips into melodrama.

catalog.title: Sleepy Hollow
catalog.hook: In 1799 a squeamish New York constable is sent upstate to investigate a string of beheadings blamed on a headless horseman.
catalog.caution: It is gorgeous and goofy; the mystery is thin and Depp plays Ichabod as a nervous comedian.

catalog.title: Gone Girl
catalog.hook: On their fifth wedding anniversary Nick Dunne's wife disappears, and the more the town learns about their marriage, the worse he looks.
catalog.caution: Its view of marriage is acid and nobody is likable; one burst of violence is shockingly graphic.

catalog.title: Se7en
catalog.hook: A detective a week from retirement and his hot-headed replacement hunt a killer staging each murder as one of the seven deadly sins.
catalog.caution: It is relentlessly grim, the crime scenes are grotesque, and the ending is famous for a reason.

catalog.title: Zodiac
catalog.hook: A cartoonist, a reporter and two detectives spend decades obsessed with the Zodiac killer in San Francisco.
catalog.caution: It is over two and a half hours of procedure and it does not solve the case; obsession is the subject.

catalog.title: Prisoners
catalog.hook: When his young daughter and her friend vanish on Thanksgiving, a father takes the investigation into his own hands.
catalog.caution: It is long, cold and morally queasy, with a torture subplot at its centre.

catalog.title: Parasite
catalog.hook: A poor family in a semi-basement scheme their way, one by one, into jobs with a wealthy family in their architect-designed house.
catalog.caution: It turns sharply in the second half, and the ending is violent and bitter.

catalog.title: Knives Out
catalog.hook: When a wealthy crime novelist is found dead after his eighty-fifth birthday, a Southern gentleman detective interviews his grasping family.
catalog.caution: It is a puzzle and a comedy; if you dislike whodunits that show their hand early, the structure may annoy you.

catalog.title: Glass Onion
catalog.hook: A tech billionaire invites his old friends to his private Greek island for a murder-mystery weekend, and Benoit Blanc turns up uninvited.
catalog.caution: It is broader and longer than the first, and the satire is about as subtle as its villain.

catalog.title: The Talented Mr. Ripley
catalog.hook: In 1958 a young man is paid to bring a rich heir home from Italy, and falls in love with the life, and the heir.
catalog.caution: Tom's choices are hard to watch and the ending leaves him exactly where you fear.

catalog.title: Rear Window
catalog.hook: Laid up with a broken leg, a photographer starts watching his neighbours across the courtyard and becomes sure one of them has killed his wife.
catalog.caution: It is one room and a lot of talk for the first hour; the tension is all slow pressure.

catalog.title: Vertigo
catalog.hook: A retired detective with a fear of heights is hired to follow an old friend's wife, who seems to be possessed by a dead woman.
catalog.caution: It is slow, strange and obsessive, and Scottie's behaviour towards Judy is deeply uncomfortable.

catalog.title: Promising Young Woman
catalog.hook: By night, Cassie pretends to be blackout drunk in bars to see which nice guys take her home, and her revenge on the past is only beginning.
catalog.caution: It is sugar-coloured but bitter, and its ending is deliberately upsetting.

catalog.title: Black Swan
catalog.hook: A perfectionist ballerina is cast as the Swan Queen and, chasing the darker Black Swan, starts to crack.
catalog.caution: It is claustrophobic and paranoid; the self-harm and body horror are close and frequent.

catalog.title: Saltburn
catalog.hook: A scholarship student at Oxford is invited to spend the summer at his glamorous friend's family estate.
catalog.caution: It is designed to provoke, several scenes exist mainly to shock, and the final reveal explains everything twice.

catalog.title: Nightcrawler
catalog.hook: A driven loner discovers the business of filming crime scenes for local TV news in Los Angeles, and is very good at it.
catalog.caution: Lou is repellent from the first scene and the film never asks you to like him.

catalog.title: Oldboy
catalog.hook: A man is kidnapped and kept in a hotel room for fifteen years without explanation, then released, with five days to find out why.
catalog.caution: Its final revelation is one of cinema's most disturbing, and there is real cruelty to animals on screen.

catalog.title: The Handmaiden
catalog.hook: In 1930s Korea a pickpocket is placed as maid to a Japanese heiress to help a con man seduce her, and falls for her instead.
catalog.caution: It is long, told three times from different angles, and very sexually explicit.
comps: Portrait of a Lady on Fire

catalog.title: Memento
catalog.hook: A man who cannot form new memories hunts his wife's killer using tattoos, Polaroids and notes, told backwards.
catalog.caution: The structure demands attention; tune out for five minutes and it is hard to catch up.

catalog.title: Shutter Island
catalog.hook: In 1954 two US marshals arrive at a hospital for the criminally insane on an island off Boston to find a patient who has vanished from a locked cell.
catalog.caution: If you see the twist coming, the long middle drags, and its subject matter is very heavy.

catalog.title: Fargo
catalog.hook: A desperate Minneapolis car salesman hires two criminals to kidnap his wife, and a very pregnant, very polite police chief starts to unpick it.
catalog.caution: The violence arrives in sudden ugly bursts amid the deadpan; the tone takes a moment to tune into.

catalog.title: No Country for Old Men
catalog.hook: A hunter finds two million dollars at a drug deal gone wrong in West Texas, and a killer with a captive bolt pistol follows him.
catalog.caution: It denies you the ending a thriller promises, on purpose.

catalog.title: Pulp Fiction
catalog.hook: Two hitmen, a boxer, a gangster's wife and a pair of diner robbers cross paths in Los Angeles, out of order.
catalog.caution: It is long and talky, the timeline jumps, and it includes a male rape scene.

catalog.title: Kill Bill: Vol. 1
catalog.hook: A bride shot at her own wedding wakes from a four-year coma and starts crossing names off a list.
catalog.caution: It is half a story; the revenge is spectacular and the motive is mostly saved for part two.
contentWarnings: sexual assault of a comatose woman

catalog.title: Kill Bill: Vol. 2
catalog.hook: The Bride finishes the list, and finally meets Bill.
catalog.caution: It is slower and talkier than the first, and its climax is a conversation.

catalog.title: Mad Max: Fury Road
catalog.hook: In the wasteland, Imperator Furiosa drives a war rig full of the warlord's escaped wives across the desert, and a captured drifter is chained to the front of the pursuit.
catalog.caution: It is essentially one two-hour chase; if you need dialogue and plot, there is very little.
catalog.leadNote: Furiosa drives the story; Max mostly rides along

catalog.title: John Wick
catalog.hook: A retired hitman is mourning his wife when the son of a Russian mobster steals his car and kills the puppy she left him.
catalog.caution: The puppy is killed on screen early; and the story is a thin wire for the fights.

catalog.title: The Matrix
catalog.hook: A hacker called Neo is contacted by a woman called Trinity, and told the world he lives in is a simulation.
catalog.caution: Its look has been copied so often it may feel familiar, and the exposition in the middle is heavy.

catalog.title: Blade Runner
catalog.hook: In rainy 2019 Los Angeles a burned-out cop is ordered to hunt four replicants who have come back to Earth looking for their maker.
catalog.caution: It is slow, moody and more interested in atmosphere than action; one 'romance' scene is coercive.

catalog.title: Arrival
catalog.hook: When twelve alien ships appear over the Earth, a linguist is recruited to work out what the visitors are trying to say.
catalog.caution: It is a quiet film about language and grief; the aliens never become a threat to fight.
contentWarnings: death of a child from illness

catalog.title: Ex Machina
catalog.hook: A programmer wins a week at his reclusive boss's mountain estate and is asked to judge whether a robot named Ava is truly conscious.
catalog.caution: It is three people in a glass house talking; the tension is cerebral until the last ten minutes.

catalog.title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
catalog.hook: A laundromat owner being audited by the IRS learns she must connect with infinite versions of herself to save the multiverse.
catalog.caution: It is maximalist and chaotic, with hot-dog fingers and butt plugs; if absurdity tires you, it is a long two hours.

catalog.title: Interstellar
catalog.hook: On a dying Earth, a former pilot leaves his children to fly through a wormhole looking for a new home for humanity.
catalog.caution: It is nearly three hours, the science talk is dense, and the sound mix buries some dialogue.

catalog.title: Dune
catalog.hook: The heir of House Atreides goes with his family to rule the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the most valuable substance in the universe.
catalog.caution: It is the first half of the story and ends mid-stride; much of it is setup and staring at sand.
comps: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring

catalog.title: Dune: Part Two
catalog.hook: Paul joins the Fremen of the deep desert and rides the line between revenge and the holy war he has foreseen.
catalog.caution: It is long and heavy with prophecy, and its hero's arc is deliberately troubling.

catalog.title: Edge of Tomorrow
catalog.hook: A cowardly PR officer is thrown into a beach invasion against aliens, dies, and wakes up the morning before, again.
catalog.caution: It is a crowd-pleaser with a weaker final act than its middle.
catalog.leadNote: Emily Blunt's Rita is the war hero he has to become

catalog.title: The Princess Bride
catalog.hook: A grandfather reads his grandson the story of Buttercup and Westley: true love, a giant, a swordsman with a grudge, and Rodents of Unusual Size.
catalog.caution: It is gentle and knowing; if you want swashbuckling played straight, the jokes win.

catalog.title: Stardust
catalog.hook: A young man crosses the wall out of his English village to bring back a fallen star for the girl he loves, and the star is a woman.
catalog.caution: It is busy, with three plots chasing each other, and some of the humour is broad.

catalog.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
catalog.hook: A hobbit inherits a ring that would let its maker rule the world, and sets out to destroy it with eight companions.
catalog.caution: It is three hours and the start of a nine-hour story; the Shire opening is slow.
comps: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers

catalog.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
catalog.hook: The fellowship is broken: two hobbits head for Mordor with Gollum, and the rest are drawn into the war at Helm's Deep.
catalog.caution: It is a middle chapter with no beginning or end of its own.
comps: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring

prerequisite.needsTitle: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring

catalog.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
catalog.hook: Frodo and Sam reach Mount Doom as the armies of the West march on the Black Gate to buy them time.
catalog.caution: It ends several times; the epilogue alone is longer than some short films.
comps: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers

prerequisite.needsTitle: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers

catalog.title: Spirited Away
catalog.hook: A sulky ten-year-old moving house wanders into a spirit world, where her parents are turned into pigs and she has to work in a bathhouse for the gods.
catalog.caution: It runs on dream logic; if you need the rules explained, Miyazaki does not.

catalog.title: Princess Mononoke
catalog.hook: A cursed young prince travels west and finds himself between an ironworks town and the forest gods, and the wolf girl, at war with it.
catalog.caution: It is far more violent than most Ghibli, with severed limbs, and its sympathies are complicated.

catalog.title: Howl's Moving Castle
catalog.hook: A young hatmaker cursed into the body of an old woman takes refuge as the cleaner in a wandering castle owned by a vain wizard.
catalog.caution: The plot dissolves in the second half and the war story is never quite explained.

catalog.title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
catalog.director: Bob Persichetti, Peter Ramsey and Rodney Rothman
catalog.hook: Brooklyn teenager Miles Morales gets bitten by a radioactive spider the same week a collider brings Spider-People from other dimensions into his.
catalog.caution: It is visually dense to the point of overload, and it is a superhero origin at heart.
comps: Puss in Boots: The Last Wish

catalog.title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
catalog.hook: Jack Skellington, Pumpkin King of Halloween Town, is tired of scaring and decides to take over Christmas.
catalog.caution: It is short and a musical; if songs are not for you, a third of it will not be either.

catalog.title: Labyrinth
catalog.hook: A teenager wishes the goblins would take her baby brother, and the Goblin King obliges, giving her thirteen hours to solve his labyrinth.
catalog.caution: It is puppets and Bowie songs; the plot is a string of encounters.

catalog.title: The Shape of Water
catalog.hook: In 1962 a mute cleaner at a government lab falls in love with the amphibian man held captive there.
catalog.caution: It is a fairy tale that commits fully to the romance, which some find sweet and others absurd.

catalog.title: Practical Magic
catalog.hook: Two witch sisters raised by their aunts, under a curse that kills the men they love, have to hide a body that will not stay dead.
catalog.caution: It cannot decide whether it is a romcom or a horror film and the tonal shifts are sharp.

catalog.title: Hocus Pocus
catalog.hook: On Halloween in Salem a teenager lights a candle that brings back three seventeenth-century witch sisters who need children to stay young.
catalog.caution: It is a family comedy; adults will enjoy the Sanderson sisters and little else.

catalog.title: Edward Scissorhands
catalog.hook: An Avon lady finds a gentle artificial man with scissors for hands alone in a castle and brings him home to her pastel suburb.
catalog.caution: It is a simple fable and the townsfolk are cartoon villains.

catalog.title: Pride & Prejudice
catalog.hook: The second of five unmarried Bennet sisters meets the proud Mr Darcy and decides she cannot stand him.
catalog.caution: It is a condensed Austen; purists miss subplots and the second ending.
comps: Portrait of a Lady on Fire

catalog.title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
catalog.hook: In 1770 a painter is hired to paint a reluctant bride's wedding portrait in secret on a Breton island.
catalog.caution: It is slow, quiet and subtitled, and its romance builds in glances.

catalog.title: Before Sunrise
catalog.hook: A young American and a French student meet on a train and spend one night walking around Vienna before he flies home.
catalog.caution: Nothing happens but talk; if you need plot, it is ninety minutes of conversation.

catalog.title: When Harry Met Sally...
catalog.hook: Over twelve years in New York, two people who agreed men and women cannot be friends keep running into each other.
catalog.caution: It is very 1989, and its central question has dated as much as its knitwear.

catalog.title: Crazy Rich Asians
catalog.hook: An economics professor goes to Singapore for her boyfriend's best friend's wedding and discovers his family is extraordinarily rich and his mother disapproves.
catalog.caution: It is a classic romcom template; the surprises are in the setting and the cast, not the story.

catalog.title: Titanic
catalog.hook: A seventeen-year-old engaged to a cruel millionaire falls for a penniless artist aboard the Titanic's maiden voyage.
catalog.caution: It is over three hours and the dialogue is broad; the sinking is the last hour and a half.

catalog.title: Phantom Thread
catalog.hook: A fastidious 1950s London dressmaker takes a young waitress as his muse and lover, and she does not intend to be discarded like the others.
catalog.caution: It is mannered and quiet and its romance is decidedly odd.
comps: Portrait of a Lady on Fire

catalog.title: Clueless
catalog.hook: A rich, well-meaning Beverly Hills teenager makes over the new girl at school and plays matchmaker for everyone except herself.
catalog.caution: It is light as air and very 1995; there is no more to it than charm.

catalog.title: Mean Girls
catalog.hook: Homeschooled in Africa until now, Cady starts at an Illinois high school and infiltrates its most powerful clique.
catalog.caution: It is a teen comedy with a tidy moral; it is sharper than most and still very much of 2004.

catalog.title: Bridesmaids
catalog.hook: A broke baker in Milwaukee is made maid of honour for her best friend's wedding and competes with the bride's perfect new friend.
catalog.caution: It runs long for a comedy and the gross-out scenes are very gross.

catalog.title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
catalog.hook: Between the wars, the concierge of a grand Alpine hotel and his lobby boy are drawn into the theft of a priceless painting and a murder.
catalog.caution: If Wes Anderson's symmetry and deadpan do not charm you, this is the most Wes Anderson of all.
contentWarnings: a cat is thrown from a window

catalog.title: Hot Fuzz
catalog.hook: London's best police officer is transferred to a perfect English village where accidents keep happening.
catalog.caution: Several deaths are surprisingly gory for a comedy, and it is long for one.

catalog.title: Death Becomes Her
catalog.hook: Two rivals for the same man both drink a potion of eternal youth, and then try to kill each other.
catalog.caution: It is a broad cartoon and the ending is cold; nobody here is likable.

catalog.title: Heathers
catalog.hook: Veronica is tired of her clique of three girls called Heather, and the new boy at school has a way of making problems disappear.
catalog.caution: Its black comedy is about teen suicide and murder, and the jokes are very dark.

catalog.title: The Godfather
catalog.hook: The aging head of a New York crime family survives an assassination attempt, and his youngest son, the one who wanted out, steps in.
catalog.caution: It is nearly three hours and deliberately paced, and it shows its women very little interest.

catalog.title: Whiplash
catalog.hook: A first-year jazz drummer at a cutthroat music conservatory is picked for the band run by a brilliant, abusive conductor.
catalog.caution: It is intense and the abuse is unrelenting; there is no warmth to hide in.

catalog.title: Little Women
catalog.hook: Jo March, a struggling writer in New York, remembers growing up with her three sisters in Concord during the Civil War.
catalog.caution: It jumps between two timelines, which can be confusing until the colour grading clicks.
contentWarnings: death of a sister from illness

catalog.title: Lady Bird
catalog.hook: A Sacramento high-school senior who calls herself Lady Bird battles her mother through her final year before college.
catalog.caution: It is small and episodic; nothing dramatic happens.

catalog.title: Past Lives
catalog.hook: Two childhood friends separated when one emigrates from Seoul reconnect online twelve years later, and again in New York twelve years after that.
catalog.caution: It is quiet and restrained to the point of stillness; the drama is all unsaid.
comps: Portrait of a Lady on Fire

catalog.title: Murder on the Orient Express
catalog.hook: When an American passenger is stabbed in his compartment on the snowbound Orient Express, Hercule Poirot interviews everyone aboard.
catalog.caution: It is a stately, talky whodunit; the interviews take the whole middle.
contentWarnings: a child's kidnapping in the backstory

catalog.title: Clue
catalog.hook: Six blackmail victims are invited to a remote mansion in 1954 under false names, and their host turns up dead.
catalog.caution: It is pure farce; the mystery is a joke delivery system.

catalog.title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
catalog.hook: In 1936 archaeologist Indiana Jones races the Nazis to find the Ark of the Covenant.
catalog.caution: Indy's past with Marion is uncomfortable by modern standards, and the climax melts faces.

catalog.title: Jurassic Park
catalog.hook: A billionaire invites scientists to preview his island park of cloned dinosaurs, and the power goes out.
catalog.caution: The science lecture in the first half is long, and the kids are in serious peril.

catalog.title: The Mummy
catalog.hook: In 1926 a librarian, her brother and an American legionnaire dig up the city of the dead and wake a cursed priest.
catalog.caution: It is cheesy, and its Egyptians are mostly villains or comic relief.
comps: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl

catalog.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
catalog.hook: A blacksmith teams up with an eccentric pirate to rescue the governor's daughter from a crew of cursed skeleton pirates.
catalog.caution: It is long and Jack Sparrow's act is either the reason to watch or the reason to stop.

catalog.title: Coco
catalog.hook: On the Day of the Dead, a boy who dreams of music in a family that has banned it ends up in the Land of the Dead.
catalog.caution: It is a family film built to make you cry, and it will.

catalog.title: Paprika
catalog.hook: A device that lets therapists enter patients' dreams is stolen, and dreams start leaking into the waking world.
catalog.caution: It is dense, surreal and hard to follow on a first watch.

catalog.title: Perfect Blue
catalog.hook: A pop idol quits her group to become an actress and finds herself stalked by a fan and by an online diary that seems to know her better than she does.
catalog.caution: It is an adult film, not a cartoon, with a graphic and upsetting staged rape scene.

catalog.title: Puss in Boots: The Last Wish
catalog.hook: Down to the last of his nine lives and hunted by a wolf who is Death himself, Puss sets out to find the Wishing Star.
catalog.caution: It is a kids' film first, but its fear of death is real.
